### This is a beta release

This build is for testing only. It is published as a pre-release, so it is not offered to
existing installations through the in-app updater — install it by hand from the assets below.

### Coming from the stable release

This line of betas changes how a computer identifies itself, which renames every host once.
Paired hosts still hold the old name, so remove each host on both computers and pair them again
with the same pairing password. If you already installed beta.2, nothing further is needed.

### Fixes

- A shared display can be removed again. Removing asked the system to find the display first and
  refused when it could not, so the displays you most want gone — asleep, showing another host, or
  reporting an identity this computer no longer recognises — were the only ones that could not go.
  A shared display nothing can see now gets a row of its own, since it appeared nowhere to act on.
- Removing the only display you can control no longer puts it straight back. The one-time
  automatic pick ran whenever the shared list was empty, which stopped meaning "nothing chosen
  yet" the moment you chose. It now runs only before the list has ever been decided.
- A merge can be undone. The setting existed and its wording was translated, but no control ever
  appeared for it, so a merge made by mistake could not be taken back — and the absorbed identity,
  no longer a shared display in its own right, had no row to act on either.

### Known limitations

- Undoing a merge leaves the inputs and notes that merging folded into the display the other
  identity joined, and does not make that identity a shared display again.
- Merging only syncs between hosts running this version.
- The macOS DMG is ad-hoc signed but not notarized with an Apple Developer ID, so Gatekeeper may
  require manual approval.

### What to test

- Remove a shared display and confirm it stays removed, including when it is the only one you can
  control and when the display is switched to another host.
- Merge two identities of one display, then undo the merge and confirm both parts work.
- Pair both computers and confirm their host cards run in the same order.
